frontier.hypothesis: a REAL duplicated statement inside the loop's DO-WHILE body — same-computation of `base_addr + word_offset` binding to a fresh local — could lift base_addr's reg_n_refs past CSE (which does not eliminate independent lexical uses when they are separated by clobbering intervening stores/calls)
frontier.mechanism: [[duplicated-statement-into-arms]] 2026-07-01 sanction: bytes-neutral duplication that survives CSE via intervening `efc_buki_draw_zanzou` call clobber, lifting reg_n_refs for global-RA tiebreaker; requires layer-2 review + FAKE annotation per the rule if the duplicate has no observable behaviour
frontier.next_probe: s4 (structural or judge-request): duplicate `new_var = base_addr + (((u32)word)>>2)<<2;` into a second lexical position in the loop body (before AND after the call is bytes-neutral if the second assignment is dead-stored to a new named local, but that is a cheat spelling; alternative: use base_addr in a legitimate additional computation — e.g. pass `base_addr` as a spare arg or use it in a bounds check that is dead after DCE but survives to reg-alloc). Even the cleanest form here likely needs a judge ruling on whether it is a real duplication (sanctioned) vs a dead reference (cheat).

frontier.hypothesis: a PERM_* directed permuter campaign over the base_addr/p init chain + type variants can search the RA tiebreaker space more broadly than the ~10 manual probes across s1-s3
frontier.mechanism: auto-search sampling per [[permuter-directives]] + [[permuter-fresh-seed-discipline]]; the residual is a single-insn RA tie and matches the shape permuter is designed for
frontier.next_probe: s4 (permuter modality): build permuter workspace seeded with the s3 candidate form; PERM_VAR / PERM_INT_TYPE / PERM_LINESWAP over base_addr and p; fresh-seed budget ~20-30 per macro; vet every closing form against the cheat catalog

frontier.hypothesis: buf[8] can be legitimized via the [[dead-vars-local-array]] 2026-07-01 WRITTEN-never-read carve-out if the loop body contains a matched dead store into buf[k] that pairs with target's `sw v0,0x10(sp)` in the jal delay slot
frontier.mechanism: the target dead-store discipline: pair a source-level `buf[k] = ...` store with the target byte, satisfying the WRITTEN carve-out; the store must be dead (no reload)
frontier.next_probe: s4 (structural/judge-request): try `buf[4] = efc_buki_draw_zanzou(new_var, ...);` (capture the discarded return into the array slot at sp+0x10 — buf[4] since buf is s32) and measure; requires cheat-reviewer judgment on whether this qualifies under the 2026-07-01 carve-out without a matched dead store already being present in target
